primary_sources_opened.authors: Se-Young Yun, Jinwoo Shin, Yung Yi

primary_sources_opened.matched: arbitrary conflict graph; local instantaneous channel; finite-state irreducible continuous-time Markov channel; adaptive CSMA

primary_sources_opened.title: Distributed Medium Access Over Time-Varying Channels
primary_sources_opened.authors: Se-Young Yun, Jinwoo Shin, Yung Yi
primary_sources_opened.read_sections: PDF pages 1-4 and 9; Theorem 4.2 and equation (32) also visually read in rendered page 9
primary_sources_opened.model: independent Bernoulli slot arrivals; positive finite channel levels; irreducible continuous-time finite-state Markov channels; arbitrary graph; collision-free instantaneous carrier sensing
primary_sources_opened.theorem: Theorem 4.2: equation (32) is throughput optimal. Definition 2.1 explicitly defines throughput optimality using rate stability, D_i(t)/t -> lambda_i almost surely.
primary_sources_opened.queue_rule: f_i^(t)(x)=exp(2 n c_max w(Q_max(floor t)) + x r_i(t)); g_i^(t)(x)=exp(2 n c_max w(Q_max(floor t))); r_i(t)=max{w(Q_i(floor t)),sqrt(w(Q_max(floor t)))}; w(x)=log log(x+e).
primary_sources_opened.information: Global Qmax may be replaced by a distributed approximation; the paper says this does not alter rate stability. The theorem proof is assigned to supplementary material, not fully reproduced in the opened main-paper text.
primary_sources_opened.status: Closest primary result verified here; not represented as the latest result in the entire literature or as a finite-mean-queue theorem.
